newsitem.title: UK: LME copper floats above $2,500, lead surges.
newsitem.headline: LME copper floats above $2,500, lead surges.

text.p: LME copper extended its rally on Wednesday morning, squeezing up to a fresh one-year high, but traders were wary of the future direction.
Most of the other metals chalked up gains with copper, but lead woke from its recent slumber and charged higher.
Three month copper prices touched a peak of $2,516, up $23 from Tuesday's kerb close, but after a brief flurry early on the pre-market, turnover was moderate during official trading.
It ended the morning kerb at $2,307.
"At the moment, I don't think we have a lot more on the upside," one floor trader said.

A wave of fund buying and short-covering swept prices out of negative territory on Tuesday afternoon during a heated $50 rally, but it left the market overbought, with the 14-day RSI at 78 on Wednesday.
Copper supplies are tight and LME stocks fell by 1,125 tonnes on Wednesday, resuming sizeable drawdowns after a modest decline of 475 tonnes on Tuesday.
Supply is also under threat, with labour problems dogging operations in Chile.

Borrowing boosted spreads, with the benchmark cash/threes moving out to a $80 backwardation from $70/$75 on Tuesday evening and $50 on Tuesday morning. At the end of the kerb it was indicated at $72/$82.

Interest was shown in nearby dates as well as in forwards extending to the first quarter of 1998. The July/August spread was one pocket of tightness at about a $48 backwardation, and threes/October traded at a $90 backwardation.
Aluminium was also helped by borrowing, tightening the cash/threes from a $19 contago on Tuesday afternoon to $14.
"I think someone is short in July and just needed to cover," a floor trader said.
Three month prices recovered, regaining the key $1,650 technical area and breaching the 10-day moving average at $1,661 to hit $1,668. It ended the kerb $13 higher at $1,660.
Several analysts had expected prices to test support at $1,637 or even $1,616. Resistance is pegged at $1,680, the top of its recent range.
Lead shot higher, breaking out of a price band and hitting the highest level since April 10.
Prices touched $648 after one broker began buying in a market that had been lacklustre, catching players on the hop and triggering stops above $640.
It ended the morning at $645, up $25 or four percent.
Zinc added to Tuesday's gains, bettering the May 15 recent peak by $1 at $1,359. It ended the session $5 up from Tuesday at $1,358.
The upside may be capped by an overbought market, with the 14-day RSI at 73, analysts said.
Nickel showed little enthusiasm to stray very far, holding in a narrow range and finishing $10 firmer at $7,700.
Tin was very quiet, last indicated at $5,780/90, little different from Tuesday's $5,790.
Alloy finished $5 firmer at $1,510/15.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
